before: I found the therapist, Daja, years later, randomly, and gave it a shot, although I didn't think I needed it. But she did actually help me see some things more clearly. For example, she had me write down how many people I could fully trust as a child (lots), then how many people I could fully trust as an adult (zero). That was difficult, and it's actually the opposite of what you might expect from inner-child therapy, since usually that's about people who had problems trusting as a child.
after: [an image: The study chart, an illustrated one-page map of the whole method titled "Inner Child Reparenting: The Study Chart" ("The child does not heal itself. The present-day adult learns to relate, protect, and guide."). Its panels: five practical tools (gentle self-hypnosis and meditation; journaling and dialogue; somatic and trauma therapies such as SE, EMDR, EFT and brainspotting; altered states and plant medicines, "they can also get past the guards before the adult is ready. Build sober Nurturer and Protector capacity first"; professional and relational support, "Borrow adulthood. Don't surrender it."); learning to feel love (non-cruelty, then borrowed care, then love can develop); five steps for when you can't feel like the adult yet (witness, borrow one function, adult apprentice, build capacity, relationship; "The peer supports the adult; the peer does not replace the adult"); forgiveness, with self-forgiveness on the same path (responsibility, remorse, rectify, release); enough adult capacity before going deep (a checklist: can I tell where and when I am, pause before acting, compare options, stop the exercise, take a practical protective action); no clear child yet (recover preferences, experiment and play, differentiate from other people's expectations, let identity-building and reparenting happen together); catch the hook before you interpret it ("The hook is not a truth detector"); also look outward; and closing tenets, ending "You were born worthy of love. Reconnect. Reparent. Rise."] (then the h3 Don't Give the Inner Adult Away)

The r4 guide's passage (the passage this carries):
It still didn’t reach all of my inner-child material, especially my attachment to women. The self-directed inner-child therapy I tried later felt imaginary at first. San Pedro cactus, CBD tea, and sublingual mapacho cracked it open; structured sessions with an inner-child therapist deepened it.

The method now has four elements: a wounded child, three adult functions, protective parts that may stand at the door, and a bootstrap phase for people who can’t yet occupy the adult role.
